source.title: Not all solutions are created equal: An analytical dissociation of functional and representational similarity in deep linear neural networks
source.authors: Lukas Braun; Erin Grant; Andrew M. Saxe

record.file_problem: The full text is present. Its proceedings statement says ICML 2025, while the supplied metadata says 2026.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether noise robustness and generalization error constrain representations, using analyses and simulations different from the claim versions' specified methods. It does not test any listed version directly.
record.gate_note: The study reports test-error outcomes for function-preserving transformations under input and parameter noise, and states that transformations do not inflate secondary test error near zero noise. These results do not measure the random-label/generalization coexistence, interpolation-threshold width sweep, architecture comparison, optimizer or batch effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples specified by V1–V8.
record.test_reason: The study tests how function-preserving reparametrisations affect representations and noise robustness. Its own results do not test V1–V8. In particular, additive parameter-noise sensitivity is not magnitude-aware sharpness ranked against generalization gaps (V7), and post-training neuron expansion is not training wider networks to convergence (V2).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the nonlinear experiments. The broader conclusion is that function and representation are dissociable: secondary error and input-noise robustness do not require task-specific representations, whereas optimal parameter-noise robustness constrains representations in the linear analysis, with analogous robustness differences demonstrated in nonlinear MNIST networks.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes solution manifolds and function-preserving transformations, rather than the claim versions' stated label memorization, width, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or example-removal procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise type and transformation type change the test-error outcome; duplicate expansions are more robust to parameter noise than scaled and nuisance expansions.

fits_no_version.finding: On MNIST, function-preserving transformations leave near-zero-noise test error unchanged while changing robustness: input-null transformations impair input-noise robustness, and scaled, nuisance, and duplicate transformations impair parameter-noise robustness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Functionally equivalent two-layer ReLU networks can have different representations and noise robustness without different unperturbed test performance.

fits_no_version.finding: For the analysed two-layer linear networks, minimizing secondary error permits task-agnostic representations, whereas minimizing expected loss under the specified additive parameter noise selects minimum representation-norm solutions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimal secondary-dataset performance need not identify task-specific representations; optimal parameter-noise robustness can constrain them under the stated assumptions.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, Vancouver, Canada; PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The nonlinear empirical results use MNIST and 8 random initialisations; test-error values in Figures 5D–E are not numerically recoverable from the text. The study states that systematic analytical and numerical exploration of task specifics and hyperparameter choices is left for future work.
record.rows_left_out: None. Each described test-error condition from Sections 6.2–6.3 is represented; the numerical values are shown only in Figure 5.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architectures and training recipes.
Test error when networks of increasing width are trained to convergence beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers and dependence on tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across training regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because none of these measures operationalizes a listed version; this does not dispute the qualitative noise effects reported in Section 6.3. No missing result bears on a listed version. The supplied arXiv date and proceedings year conflict; publication status cannot be resolved from this text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels under the same recipes.
A width sweep past the zero-training-error interpolation threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers under stated tuning conditions.
Large versus small batch training under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: task-trained (minimal)
rows.stage_stated: trained for 30 epochs on the full MNIST training set of 50,000 images
rows.operation_detail: Measured test error under input noise for the task-trained minimal network.
rows.note: The text describes comparison outcomes for transformations but gives no numerical value for this baseline.
rows.check: A valid comparator for noise robustness, but it measures no listed version.

rows.subject: input-null
rows.size_stated: two-layer network; 1024 hidden dimensions; manipulations add twice the number of neurons
rows.stage_stated: function-preserving transformation of a network trained for 30 epochs on MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Added perturbations to input-layer weights in unobserved input directions.
rows.value: figure only; described as having a deleterious effect
rows.note: The text says only transformations in the unobserved input space have a deleterious effect under input noise.
rows.check: The stated input-noise degradation is supported, but measures no listed version. Input-null weight perturbations do not add neurons; the size description incorrectly applies the neuron-addition statement to this transformation.

rows.subject: scaled
rows.size_stated: two-layer network; 1024 hidden dimensions; manipulations add twice the number of neurons
rows.stage_stated: function-preserving transformation of a network trained for 30 epochs on MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Rescaled neuron input and output weights while preserving the network output.
rows.value: figure only; test error degrades more quickly than for minimal models
rows.note: The text groups scaled, nuisance, and duplicate expansions as degrading more quickly than minimal models.
rows.check: The stated parameter-noise degradation is supported, but does not measure V7's magnitude-scaled sharpness or its association with generalization gaps. Rescaling weights does not add neurons.

rows.subject: nuisance
rows.size_stated: two-layer network; 1024 hidden dimensions; manipulations add twice the number of neurons
rows.stage_stated: function-preserving transformation of a network trained for 30 epochs on MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Added nuisance neurons with random incoming weights and zero outgoing weights.
rows.value: figure only; test error degrades more quickly than for minimal models
rows.note: The text groups scaled, nuisance, and duplicate expansions as degrading more quickly than minimal models.
rows.check: The stated parameter-noise degradation is supported, but measures no listed version. Adding nuisance neurons after training does not test V2.

rows.subject: duplicate
rows.size_stated: two-layer network; 1024 hidden dimensions; manipulations add twice the number of neurons
rows.stage_stated: function-preserving transformation of a network trained for 30 epochs on MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Duplicated neurons and halved the outgoing weights of each original and duplicate.
rows.value: figure only; degrades more slowly than the scaled and nuisance expansions, but more quickly than minimal models
rows.note: The text says duplicate expansions are more robust due to noise averaging, while non-minimal duplicate models still degrade more quickly than minimal ones.
rows.check: Duplication degrades test error faster than the minimal baseline but is more robust than the other expansions. This is not a partial instance of any listed version; post-training duplication does not test V2.

rows.subject: input-null
rows.size_stated: two-layer network; 1024 hidden dimensions; manipulations add twice the number of neurons
rows.stage_stated: function-preserving transformation of a network trained for 30 epochs on MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Added perturbations to input-layer weights in unobserved input directions.
rows.value: figure only; text says input-nullspace perturbations have no effect
rows.note: The text attributes the absence of effect to transformations being in unobserved input directions and input noise being absent.
rows.check: The reported absence of an input-null transformation penalty under parameter noise is supported, but measures no listed version. Input-null perturbations do not add neurons.

rows.subject: task-trained and function-preserving transformed two-layer ReLU networks
rows.size_stated: 1024 hidden dimensions; manipulations add twice the number of neurons
rows.stage_stated: trained for 30 epochs on the full MNIST training set of 50,000 images
rows.operation_detail: Compared secondary (test) error at near-zero noise across minimal and function-preserving expanded parametrisations.
rows.value: figure only; text says no manipulations inflate it
rows.note: The study reports an aggregate textual result across the manipulations; no numerical values are supplied in the text.
rows.check: The text supports unchanged near-zero-noise test error across transformations, but this measures no listed version. Only parameter-adding transformations receive the appendix's neuron-addition description.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
